The Alliance Party is proud to unveil an ambitious, modern housing policy designed to bring our national housing infrastructure into the twenty-first century. Alliance Party housing spokesperson and candidate for Palmerston North, Joshua Moss, said the policy was founded primarily on one overarching principle:

[Download the full Housing Policy (PDF, 6 pages)](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-housing-policy-2026.pdf)

> “Every human being has the right to a warm, safe, and secure home at a fair price. Through four decades of neglect, privatisation, and inaction we have failed to maintain or improve the provision of public housing. We will reverse this trend.”

The centrepiece of the Alliance policy is a five-year housing plan: a massive public building programme led by Kāinga Ora, alongside a newly established Ministry of Works, to build the homes and infrastructure Aotearoa New Zealand needs.

# Alliance Party Commits to 65 Retirement Age, Funding Aged Care Support, Supercharging KiwiSaver

## Full text (verbatim)

The Alliance Party has released its Retirement and Aged Care Policy, which keeps the pension universal, lifts the couple rate to the highest level the law allows, and commits to ending the asset test for rest home care.

[Download the full policy (PDF, 6 pages) ↓](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-retirement-and-aged-care-policy-2026.pdf)

The Alliance’s health spokesperson, Ethan Gullery, says too many people spend their whole working life saving for retirement only to end up losing their independence.

> “People spend their whole life working and saving to own their home, and then they end up having to spend it on care before the state will help.”

Under current policy, a person is only entitled to government funding for rest home care once their assets, including the family home, have fallen to $300,811. With care costing around $1,500 a week, someone whose home and other assets are worth $650,000 would pay for about four and a half years of care before the state contributes.

Mr Gullery says Super already shows a better way to do it.

“We don’t means test Super. Everyone gets it, and that’s a big part of why it’s survived. Long-term care should work on the same basis.”

The policy includes a long-term approach to supercharge KiwiSaver into a true superannuation fund, completing the promise of the 1974 Superannuation Act. The first step includes a $10,000 endowment to new KiwiSaver accounts, ringfenced for retirement or terminal illness.

“The repeal of the Superannuation Act in 1975 was one of the worst economic decisions ever made in this country, and we have been playing catch up as a nation ever since. The best time to set up a superannuation system that works was decades ago – the second best time is now. As no one else will take up the mantle of forward-thinking people like Norman Kirk, the Alliance Party will do so proudly.”

Norman Kirk speaking outside Labour Party headquarters, Levin, 1972. [Chronicle / Horowhenua Historical Society Inc.](https://horowhenua.kete.net.nz/item/5d6873eb-eef2-4db1-9cb2-c0cd3afa8f2b) [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/).

“Our changes to KiwiSaver will take decades to bear fruit in full, but will ensure future generations are supported to live in dignity and security through their retirement.”

The Alliance Party also promises to increase New Zealand Superannuation for couples to 72.5 per cent of the after-tax average wage. Parliament put that upper limit in the law. The Alliance would use it, and adjust Super every quarter.

The policy also:

- Keeps the age of entitlement for Super at 65
- Funds independent advocates to support older people dealing with agencies and providers
- Sets up a dedicated Ministry for Senior Citizens

> “We are a workers’ party,” says Mr Gullery. “And after working most of their lives, workers deserve the security of knowing that they can enjoy a healthy and happy retirement without the fear of financial insecurity.”

For more information contact Alliance Party health spokesperson and [Christchurch East candidate Ethan Gullery](/candidates/christchurch-east/) on [021 318 633](tel:+6421318633) or [ethan.gullery@allianceparty.nz](mailto:ethan.gullery@allianceparty.nz)

# Alliance Party: Redistribute Power, Honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi, Move Forward in Unity

## Full text (verbatim)

The Alliance Party has released its Te Tiriti o Waitangi, Democracy, and Constitutional policy which aims to redistribute power to ordinary people by advancing constitutional transformation with Te Tiriti o Waitangi at the centre.

[Download the full policy (PDF, 9 pages) ↓](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/alliance-te-tiriti-democracy-constitutional-policy-2026.pdf)

Alliance Party president and constitutional spokesperson Tom Roud says the policy builds on the party’s commitment to redistribution of more than wealth alone.

> “Our policies tend to deal with immediate, material needs of ordinary Kiwis with an emphasis on the redistribution of wealth in this country. Redistribution of wealth without a rebalance of power would represent a gilded cage for working people, so we want to go further,” he says.

The policy is built on the principles of popular sovereignty, participatory democracy, social justice, and upholding Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

“The Alliance Party and the workers movement in general have a proud history of standing with Māori in their struggle with the Crown to address the criminal attacks on mana motuhake, tino rangatiratanga, and breaches of Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Our re-established party pays respect to our own whakapapa, and our previous relationship with the political party Mana Motuhake has provided us with a legacy of sound policy that respects Māori rights,” Mr Roud says.

On democratic issues the policy supports lowering the threshold for entering parliament and establishing processes for the recall of elected candidates by their electors.

“We are proud to be a radically democratic party that would see a system where no vote is wasted, where power does not become entrenched through custom and practice, and where elected officials are not given a few years of power without any recourse for voters to oust them if they so wish.”

> “Accountability can’t just happen every few years at the ballot box, it is a relationship that our politicians must be expected to maintain. If they can’t manage that, voters should be able to remove them from office,” Mr Roud says.

The Alliance supports advancing a written constitution, designed by the people of Aotearoa New Zealand through participatory democracy, and enshrining the constitutional status of Te Tiriti o Waitangi.

“The Matike Mai report was an enormous step forward for a serious constitutional conversation in this country. Tangata whenua have provided a framework, and now the rest of the country must come along for the conversation.”

“These are not easy subjects to cover, they take courage and a spirit of kotahitanga (unity) if we are going to come into our own as a country.”

“I am a republican, my neighbour may be a constitutional monarchist, how will we reconcile this? What would ‘the Crown’ come to mean in our existing legislation if we went down a republican route? How do we ensure we honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi in any new constitutional arrangement? Is an upper chamber undemocratic, or a necessary check on power?” Mr Roud says.

“Like almost everyone in this country I am not an expert on these issues. Regardless, the Alliance Party knows these are questions that will only become more and more central to the future of the country. It is time for Aotearoa New Zealand to decide who we want to be, and work through any nervousness and fear about that together. Tūwhitia te hopo, mairangatia te angitū: feel the fear, and do it anyway.”

For more information contact Alliance Party president and constitutional spokesperson Tom Roud on [0278667683](tel:+64278667683) or [president@allianceparty.nz](mailto:president@allianceparty.nz)

# Open, Not Owned: Alliance Party Announces Trade Policy

## Full text (verbatim)

The Alliance Party has announced the first installment in its Trade Policy, which will modernise Aotearoa New Zealand’s international trade regime, protect local industries, and take a stand for human rights around the world.

Alliance Party trade spokesperson and candidate for Wellington North, Josh Harford, says international trade is rapidly becoming a race to the bottom.

> “The craven, unrestrained obsession with maximising profits serves only to destroy local industry and bring misery on populations elsewhere in the world. Manufacturing in Aotearoa New Zealand once comprised one-quarter of all economic activity. Now, it is barely one-tenth.”

The policy includes protectionist policies around manufacturing and industry to support economic sovereignty.

> “In the past three years, we have seen factory after factory close their doors, usually in order to shift production overseas. This has damaged the economies of our regional centres, worsened unemployment, and deepened generational poverty for many. We cannot be a fully-employed nation when we ship so much economic potential offshore,” Mr Harford says.

The policy includes guidelines for fair and managed trade, rather than free trade.

> “Fair trade goes hand in hand with equality. Sweatshops around the world employ women and children in forced labour conditions, exploiting poverty conditions and societal barriers.”

Mr Harford says the Alliance is not opposed to international trade, and recognises that Aotearoa New Zealand is a small market often at the end of a long and expansive supply chain.

> “We do not believe in shutting off from the world, but right now we profit from modern slavery, outsource environmentally damaging manufacturing that we still rely on, all while undermining our economic and political sovereignty.”

> “We believe in a diversified local economy: one that will take measures to protect critical industry, keep it on shore, and expand it,” Mr Harford says.

Mr Harford took aim at existing regulations:

> “We have a very weak trade framework, designed to maximise corporate profits with little regard for either domestic industry or human rights. Without a humanitarian approach to international trade and robust modern slavery legislation, we are rapidly becoming a global outlier.”

> “This government has shown great vigour in fast-tracking legislation and using urgency for policies that harm Aotearoa New Zealand. The Alliance Party would bring that gusto to updating our modern slavery legislation and cracking down on exploitation in our trade settings.”

Mr. Harford also observed that humanitarian trade policy benefits domestic workers just as much as those overseas:

> “By cracking down on bad actors and unethical practices, we remove the financial incentive to exploit. This will help to restore industry and manufacturing on our shores. We can be a powerhouse of industry, but only if we have the right settings in place to protect those industries.”

# Time to Take Back Our Power: Alliance Launches “Reverse Privatisation” Plan

## Full text (verbatim)

Decades after the fire sale of New Zealand’s national assets in the 1980s and 1990s, the Alliance has announced a comprehensive plan to restore and protect public ownership of essential services and strategic infrastructure.

The Alliance today launched its Public Ownership and Economic Democracy Policy, a “reverse privatisation” programme to progressively buy back strategic assets that were sold and protect those that remain publicly owned. The programme would be prioritised by strategic importance, with the Crown purchasing assets at fair value where appropriate.

Alliance Party leader Victor Billot says the goal is to build a resilient New Zealand where people control their own destiny.

> “Households are cutting back on heating, infrastructure is creaking, and too many essential services are treated as cash machines for private interests. This is the legacy of the failed neoliberal sell-off of New Zealand.”

Mr Billot says it is unacceptable that many New Zealanders are struggling to stay afloat from week to week.

He says a key policy is to bring the electricity system as a whole under public ownership and control, covering generation, transmission, distribution and retail, with the goal of affordable, sustainable energy for households and local industry.

Mr Billot says the Alliance would invest in publicly owned KiwiRail, move Air New Zealand from majority Crown ownership to full public ownership, and progressively restore public ownership of strategically important ports where privatisation or corporatisation has undermined public control.

> “The Alliance Party identifies the State Owned Enterprises Act as an unmitigated failure. Turning public goods and services into commercial entities for privatised profit was absurd in 1986 and it’s absurd today. We will repeal and replace this legislation so that the people of this country have the infrastructure they built and paid for work for them – not corporate shareholders.”

The Alliance would keep public water services and infrastructure in public ownership and bring monopoly telecommunications infrastructure into public ownership, including the “last mile” connections to homes and businesses.

The Alliance would create KiwiWorks, a Ministry of Works for the 21st Century, to build state housing and infrastructure, develop construction capacity and create jobs. It would also establish a Ministry of Development and a publicly owned Development Bank, and keep Kiwibank in public ownership.

Works councils would be introduced in larger enterprises, and workers would be represented on the boards of major public enterprises. The Official Information Act would be extended to Crown-controlled listed companies.

Mr Billot says the Alliance is committed to giving workers a voice in the enterprises their labour builds.

To protect economic resilience, the Crown would have a right of first refusal, depending on fiscal viability, to acquire businesses in identified critical industries facing sale or liquidation. Where necessary, it could operate them publicly or work with employees to support cooperative buyouts.

[Download the full Public Ownership and Economic Democracy Policy (PDF, 9 pages)](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/alliance-public-ownership-economic-democracy-policy-2026.pdf)

# A Commitment to Peace: Alliance Party Releases Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy

## Full text (verbatim)

The Alliance Party has released its Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy, a rebuke of the USA-centric philosophy which has skewed Aotearoa New Zealand’s international relations for the better part of eighty years. Foreign Affairs and Defence spokesperson Josh Harford said that the policy is designed to cement the country’s independence in a fractious world:

> “We are increasingly moving away from a unipolar world order determined by the capriciousness of American foreign policy. It is time to forge our own path, with the independence and security of our Pacific region front and centre.”

The policy emphasises internationalism, non-alignment, disarmament, and decolonisation. It includes support for a strong United Nations and the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone. It also reaffirms the Alliance Party’s commitment to the Sustainable Development Goals.

Mr. Harford said that one basic tenet of the policy is the right to self-determination:

> “Too many people around the world are subjected to rule through force. Whether it is nations under dictatorship, or independent people subjugated by another nation. We would use our voice to draw attention to these injustices. In the Middle East, we must demand self-determination for Palestinians and the right to return to their homeland.”

> “The Alliance Party is proud of New Zealand’s record as an internationalist nation. As a founding member of the United Nations, UNESCO, and much more, we have a proven track record as a fighter for peace, diplomacy, and stability around the world. We are a proud and committed advocate of the Sustainable Development Goals, and we have the opportunity to build on this record into the future.”

He also took aim at the brutal cycle of debt which he says cripples the Global South:

> “Developing nations should not be trapped in cycles of debt repayment that prevent them from providing basic services, investing in their people, or developing sustainable economies. Global South debt is a leading cause of corruption, poverty, and state failure.”

> “National destitution is often a direct result of colonialism and resource extraction. Developed nations, especially those who participated in exploiting other countries, have a responsibility to cancel their foreign aid debts as a form of reparation. We see the necessary link between economic and national sovereignty. One without the other is illusory, and that is as true for Aotearoa New Zealand as it is for anywhere else.”

Mr. Harford also pointed to existing US military and intelligence infrastructure in New Zealand as undermining national sovereignty:

> “As we speak, our country is providing military and political intelligence that the United States uses or provides to other powerful states, enabling atrocities around the world. Tangimoana, Waihopai, Black Birch, and Wellington’s FBI Office are used to advance the hegemony of another state, with no regard for our own national interest. We pledge to immediately terminate intelligence sharing, with a view to fully demilitarising these facilities.”

[Download the full Foreign Affairs, Defence, and International Relations Policy (PDF, 6 pages)](https://allianceparty.nz/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/alliance-foreign-affairs-defence-international-relations-policy-2026.pdf)
